name: Aim assist
summary: When the player fires roughly toward a target, send the shot at it if it is inside a small cone and in range.
what_it_does: Aiming precisely with keys, a stick or a touch screen is hard, so many games quietly correct the shot. At fire time, look for targets inside a cone around the aim direction and within range, pick the one closest by angle, and fire at it. Halo calls this auto-aim or bullet magnetism. Doom's public source aims bullets this way: it looks for a target straight ahead, then a few degrees to each side, and sets the shot's vertical angle to hit it.
use_when: Shooters with gamepad or touch input, and any game where the player can't aim freely, like this one, which only shoots left or right.
watch_out: Too wide a cone feels like the game plays itself and can pick the wrong target when several are close. Competitive players notice it.
starting_values: Doom checks about 5.6 degrees to each side (1<<26 in its angle units) before giving up. A cone of 5 to 15 degrees is a sensible starting range.
prompt:
Add aim assist to shooting.
- When the player fires, find targets within 420 px whose direction is within 10 degrees of the aim direction.
- If there are any, fire at the one with the smallest angle difference. Otherwise fire straight.
- Only change the new shot's direction. Never move the player's aim or the camera.
- Make the cone and range settings, with a way to turn it off.

Acceptance checks:
1. Firing at a target slightly above or below the aim line hits it.
2. A target more than 10 degrees off is not hit unless aimed at.
3. With assist off, shots go exactly where aimed.
